findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits before the DB requery, so a new dashboard/folder stays denied for up to 30s
findings.body: Check first consults permDenialCache and returns Allowed=false before any permission lookup. A denial is written at line 154 whenever a check fails, keyed by user, action, name and parent folder, with a 30s TTL. The PR's stated goal is that a creator can access a dashboard or folder they just created. But if the creator (or anyone) requests that resource before it exists, the denial is cached. After creation, the same Check hits the denial entry and returns false without reaching the new fallback-to-DB path. Nothing invalidates the denial entry when permissions or the resource change. The bug the PR is meant to fix therefore persists for the TTL window. The denial lookup should be skipped or invalidated when the resource is not present in the cached permissions, or the denial should not be cached for name-specific checks.

findings.title: Denial cache key concatenation is ambiguous and can collide across resources
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins action, name and parent with "_" without escaping. Resource names may contain underscores, so distinct requests produce the same key. For example name="x_y" with parent="" and name="x" with parent="y" both yield the suffix "x_y_". A cached denial for one dashboard then denies a different dashboard for the same user for 30s. Use an unambiguous separator or hash the tuple.
